verdict.rationale: Plausible can be driven without its dashboard through its own HTTP interfaces. The Stats API accepts queries via POST and returns JSON, authenticated with team-scoped API keys. The Events API records pageviews and custom events server-side. That supports headless, scriptable automation, but nothing in the evidence describes a CLI, CI integration, or a dedicated headless mode, and the OpenAPI probes all returned 404. Missing for 10: an official CLI or CI tooling (e.g. a GitHub Action), documented CI/automation workflows, a machine-readable OpenAPI spec, and hands-on corroboration of headless use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: The /api/v2/query endpoint accepts simple and complex stats queries in the POST request body and returns the metrics as JSON.
Plausible Stats API is a read-only HTTP interface for viewing historical and real-time stats.
The Plausible Events API can be used to record pageviews and custom events. This is useful when tracking Android or iOS mobile apps, or for server side tracking.
